notes: Primary contact: CTO Samir Desai. Very hands-on, wants deterministic latency for enterprise search use-case.
Business driver: replace in-house model infra that's costly to operate; need predictable TCO and strict SLAs for customers.
Workload profile: heavy reranking + embeddings on ingestion pipeline; peak daily window 10:00-14:00 PT, bursty traffic (x4 baseline).
Latency targets: p95 < 120ms for 512-token generation (search snippets), p95 < 50ms for embedding lookups (single request).
Throughput targets: sustained 120 qps for small text rerank flows, burst to 400 qps for short windows; average context 256 tokens.
Reserved GPU planning: initial ask = capacity equivalent to 6x H100 (80GB) nodes with headroom for 20% burst; ask from infra: explicit per-GPU reservation and burst pool.
Preferred model family: open LLM (quantized) tuned for search (customer prefers ability to pin versions). Wants recommendation from Redwood Optimize on quantization & kernel profiles.

Model fallback policy: primary = rtx-large-32b-qat (quantized) for quality; fallback = rtx-medium-8b-q for saturation to preserve p95 latency < 300ms and avoid 503s. Team asked for automated scoring to detect quality erosion post-fallback.

Cross-region failover needs: active-passive between us-west-2 (primary) and us-east-1 (secondary). Must support RTO < 3 minutes for routing failover. Concern: cold KV cache on failover causing initial latency spikes.

Cache strategy discussed: prefix/KV cache warming via replicated Redis (geo-replication) + asynchronous KV prefetch from primary; acceptable eventual consistency for search results (not for billing audit events).
SLA negotiation points: uptime >= 99.95% for Dedicated, separate latency SLOs with clear measurement windows (p95 over 5m and 1h). Wants credits for missed latency SLOs (sliding scale).
Operational controls they want in Console: per-model token/latency breakdown, per-route SLO dashboards, and canary rollout toggles with automatic fallback to last-known-good model.

Security/Compliance: strict data residency requirement for EU-derived customer subset; Redwood Private for EU customers is required unless hosted with region isolation and contractual residency guarantees.
Quote from CTO on call: "We will not accept silent performance regressions — need auditable eval hooks and rollback policy."

POC duration requested: 6 weeks. Key success criteria: meet throughput & latency SLOs under 80% simulated production load, successful cross-region failover drill without >5% error rate, and validated model-fallback quality with automated eval suite.
Notes on pricing: prefers committed monthly reserved capacity with burst credits; asked for blended ARR examples with H100 vs A100 mixes.
Networking constraints: strict egress caps, requires review of per-GPU bandwidth assumptions and VPC peering requirements.
History: migrated from managed endpoints last year; primary pain = unpredictable tail latency and noisy neighbors during daily ingest spikes.
AE notes (Ava): follow-up items send SLA draft + suggested reserved GPU config and Optimize report by 2026-02-24.
Technical ask (SE): include a failover runbook that covers cache warming, DNS TTLs, session affinity handling for ongoing chat sessions, and metrics to trigger rollback.
Requested artifacts by customer: load-test script (k6 + tokenized payloads), evaluation dataset for reranking validation, sample SLA wording for latency credits.
Customer asked about multi-tenant isolation on Dedicated: credit requirement = per-customer isolation on GPU pools, support for pinning noisy routes to dedicated instances.
Decision-making group: CTO + Head of Platform (Nina Park) + Procurement. Procurement timeline aggressive: legal review in 2-3 weeks after POC signoff.
Customer open to Dedicated + Private hybrid: Dedicated for global public-facing search; Private (on-prem or VPC) for EU regulated customers.
Desired contract length: 12-24 months with quarterly performance reviews and SLA KPIs.
Ask: explicit failback policy that automatically moves traffic back to primary once caches are sufficiently warmed and latencies stable for 30 minutes.
Internal red flags: they will push for lower latency SLO levels in commercial contract; must quantify cost of faster p95 targets (more reserved GPUs, higher cost).

Operational playbook ask: runbook for a 'saturation event' that includes model-variant fallback + queued degradation steps (e.g., reduce max tokens, increase quantization) — customer wants configurable policy in Console.
Requested inclusion in Contract Appendix: list of model variants allowed for fallback, clear QC thresholds for acceptable outputs, and rollback SLA language.
AE impression: high technical buy-in, procurement is gating on legal residency language + budget sign-off. Good fit for Redwood Dedicated + Optimize.
